title: A Straight Line on a Log Axis

scenes.visual: Title card 'A Straight Line on a Log Axis' over a faint grid. Same COLOUR MAP as the first film: TEAL dot or line = survivors and l_x; GREY fading dot and GREY bar = deaths. Cream background, 16:9. Every number appears only as on-screen text. Curves for Type II and Hydra are computed from a constant chance of death; the Type I and Type III shapes and the 'real cohort' line are labelled 'schematic'.

scenes.tts: In the first film, survival fed into R zero. Now watch survival alone: half of this cohort dies every year. Do the same number die each year?
scenes.caption: In the first film, survival fed into R0. Now watch survival alone: half of this cohort dies every year. Do the same number die each year?
scenes.visual: A small inset of the first film's stacked R0 bar shrinks away to the corner. A large block of TEAL dots appears, labelled '1,000 newborns' and 'chance of death each year = 0.5'.
scenes.narration: In the first film, survival fed into R0. Now watch survival alone: half of this cohort dies every year. Do the same number die each year?

scenes.tts: In the first year, half of the cohort fades to grey. The grey bar below the axis counts those deaths.
scenes.visual: Half the TEAL dots turn GREY and fade. On screen: 'alive: 500'. Below a time axis, a GREY bar for year 1 rises to '500 deaths'.
scenes.narration: In the first year, half of the cohort fades to grey. The grey bar below the axis counts those deaths.

scenes.tts: The next year, half die again, but half of a smaller group. Year after year, the grey bars shrink. A constant chance of death removes the same fraction each year, not the same number.
scenes.visual: Two more years run. TEAL counts on screen: '250', then '125'. GREY bars for years 2 and 3: '250', '125' (computed), each half the one before. A label settles under the bars: 'same fraction, shrinking numbers'.
scenes.narration: The next year, half die again, but half of a smaller group. Year after year, the grey bars shrink. A constant chance of death removes the same fraction each year, not the same number.

scenes.tts: Plot the share still alive against age, on an ordinary axis. The points fall steeply at first, then the curve bends and flattens toward zero.
scenes.visual: TEAL points at ages 0 to 3 on a linear y-axis labelled 'l_x' (1, 0.5, 0.25, 0.125; computed) are joined by a smooth TEAL curve that bends and flattens. Axis label 'ordinary axis'.
scenes.narration: Plot the share still alive against age, on an ordinary axis. The points fall steeply at first, then the curve bends and flattens toward zero.

scenes.tts: Ecologists usually plot survival on a log axis instead. On a log axis, every halving is the same step down. So equal drops mean equal fractions lost.
scenes.visual: The y-axis gridlines slide and re-space into a log scale with labels '1', '0.5', '0.25', '0.125', equally spaced, each step marked 'x 1/2'. A faint '0.1' gridline sits just below 0.125 for reference. Axis label changes to 'l_x, log axis'.
scenes.narration: Ecologists usually plot survival on a log axis instead. On a log axis, every halving is the same step down. So equal drops mean equal fractions lost.

scenes.tts: Watch the same points. They slide into a straight line. A constant chance of death draws a straight line on a log axis. This shape is called Type Two.
scenes.caption: Watch the same points. They slide into a straight line. A constant chance of death draws a straight line on a log axis. This shape is called Type II.
scenes.visual: The four TEAL points glide to their new heights and line up; a straight TEAL line is drawn through them (computed, log10 l_x falling by the same step each year). Label 'Type II: constant chance of death'.
scenes.narration: Watch the same points. They slide into a straight line. A constant chance of death draws a straight line on a log axis. This shape is called Type II.

scenes.tts: Two other shapes sit beside it. Type One stays high, then plunges, because most deaths come late. Type Three drops steeply, then flattens, because most deaths come early.
scenes.caption: Two other shapes sit beside it. Type I stays high, then plunges, because most deaths come late. Type III drops steeply, then flattens, because most deaths come early.
scenes.visual: On the same log axis, two thinner lines are drawn (labelled 'schematic'): 'Type I' flat across most of life then dropping sharply at the right; 'Type III' plunging at the left then nearly flat. Small tags mark where the deaths fall: 'deaths late', 'deaths early'.
scenes.narration: Two other shapes sit beside it. Type I stays high, then plunges, because most deaths come late. Type III drops steeply, then flattens, because most deaths come early.

scenes.tts: Here is another cohort on the log axis. Its line stays almost flat, then plunges at old ages. Is the chance of dying constant, rising, or falling with age?
scenes.visual: The three reference lines fade to faint ghosts. A new line labelled 'a cohort (schematic)' is drawn: nearly level through youth and middle age, then bending steeply down. Three buttons: 'constant', 'rising', 'falling'.
scenes.narration: Here is another cohort on the log axis. Its line stays almost flat, then plunges at old ages. Is the chance of dying constant, rising, or falling with age?

scenes.visual: Hold on the line and the three buttons. Small on-screen text 'Predict'.

scenes.tts: Rising. Few die young, and the chance of dying climbs with age, so the line bends down late. That is close to Type One.
scenes.caption: Rising. Few die young, and the chance of dying climbs with age, so the line bends down late. That is close to Type I.
scenes.visual: The 'rising' button lights. Along the line, small labels show the chance of dying growing with age (schematic). The faint Type I ghost brightens and lies almost on top of it.
scenes.narration: Rising. Few die young, and the chance of dying climbs with age, so the line bends down late. That is close to Type I.

scenes.tts: So does every animal's chance of dying rise with age? A classic reading of ageing theory said yes, for every multicellular species that breeds repeatedly.
scenes.visual: A stamp-like card 'Mortality always rises with age?' appears over the log axis. Beside it, a simple cartoon of a Hydra: a tube-shaped body with tentacles, one small bud on its side.
scenes.narration: So does every animal's chance of dying rise with age? A classic reading of ageing theory said yes, for every multicellular species that breeds repeatedly.

scenes.tts: Researchers kept more than two thousand small freshwater Hydra in the laboratory, in twelve cohorts. They checked every animal daily for deaths, and for new buds.
scenes.visual: Rows of small dishes, each with one cartoon Hydra. On screen: '2,256 Hydra', '12 cohorts', 'checked daily: deaths and buds'. A calendar flips day by day.
scenes.narration: Researchers kept more than two thousand small freshwater Hydra in the laboratory, in twelve cohorts. They checked every animal daily for deaths, and for new buds.

scenes.tts: Deaths from culture accidents were not counted as natural deaths. Those animals counted as at risk while they were watched, then left the table. That is called censoring.
scenes.visual: One dish tips over with an 'accident' icon. That animal's lifeline turns into a dashed line ending in a small bracket labelled 'censored: not a natural death'.
scenes.narration: Deaths from culture accidents were not counted as natural deaths. Those animals counted as at risk while they were watched, then left the table. That is called censoring.

scenes.tts: In ten of the twelve cohorts, the yearly chance of natural death stayed near six in a thousand. On the log axis that is a straight, nearly level line. Budding did not systematically fall with age.
scenes.caption: In ten of the twelve cohorts, the yearly chance of natural death stayed near 6 in 1,000 (0.006). On the log axis that is a straight, nearly level line. Budding did not systematically fall with age.
scenes.visual: On screen: '10 of 12 cohorts: about 0.006 per year'. A TEAL line computed from a constant 0.006 per year runs almost level across the log axis, beside the faint Type II ghost. Below, a small row of bud icons stays about the same height across ages, labelled 'fertility: no systematic fall'.
scenes.narration: In ten of the twelve cohorts, the yearly chance of natural death stayed near 6 in 1,000 (0.006). On the log axis that is a straight, nearly level line. Budding did not systematically fall with age.

scenes.tts: That holds for laboratory cohorts, under that counting rule. It does not show that Hydra are immortal, or that they live this way in ponds.
scenes.visual: Two tags clip onto the Hydra line: 'laboratory cohorts' and 'accidents censored'. Then two crossed-out cards: 'immortal' and 'same in ponds'.
scenes.narration: That holds for laboratory cohorts, under that counting rule. It does not show that Hydra are immortal, or that they live this way in ponds.

scenes.tts: So a straight line on a log axis means a constant chance of death. And a chance of death that rises with age is not universal.
scenes.visual: The three reference lines return beside the near-level Hydra line. The Type II line glows with the label 'same fraction each year'; the 'Mortality always rises with age?' card gets a small question mark struck through it.
scenes.narration: So a straight line on a log axis means a constant chance of death. And a chance of death that rises with age is not universal.

scenes.visual: End card with the Hex mascot pointing at a straight TEAL line on a log grid. Line: 'Straight on a log axis means the same fraction dies each year.'
